data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The nocturnal UHI is primarily caused by the reduction of evapotranspiration and latent heat loss in cities, and the night-time gap is larger in cities surrounded by highly vegetated, well-irrigated countryside.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If urban irrigation and green spaces are so extensive that urban evapotranspiration equals or exceeds rural evapotranspiration, the latent heat differential vanishes.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If regional aridity suppresses rural evapotranspiration, the urban-rural latent heat gap collapses.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Rural areas cool efficiently at night via evapotranspiration, which consumes energy as latent heat rather than raising surface temperatures. Urban areas, lacking vegetation and moisture due to impervious surfaces, cannot dissipate heat this way, causing relative warmth. The gap is larger when the rural surroundings have abundant moisture and vegetation, maximizing the rural latent heat sink, whereas in arid regions the rural area also lacks evapotranspiration, shrinking the gap.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
